minor.issue: HTTPException detail is a dict — clients that read response.error.code (not response.error.detail.code) will miss mission_incomplete / already_claimed / mission_not_found codes. Same pattern as iter42 game-limits note.

critical_code_review_comments: rewards_earn.py::_build_ways sorts items only by `not eligible` — the original `sort` field from earn_actions_catalog is not honoured after this sort (Python's sort is stable, so the DB `.sort('sort', 1)` order survives WITHIN each eligibility bucket, but admins editing `sort` won't see it visibly reorder eligible items alone). Confirm intent or use a two-key sort `(not eligible, c.get('sort', 999))`.

rewards_earn.py::_seed uses $setOnInsert for missions but does NOT re-apply DEFAULT_MISSIONS fields on existing rows — this is by design (admin edits survive), but means new fields added to DEFAULT_MISSIONS after first boot will silently NOT appear on already-seeded rows. Consider a versioned migration when the schema grows.

rewards_earn.py::claim_mission catches all Exception on the unique-index insert and treats it as already_claimed — a transient write error would be mis-reported. Consider narrowing to pymongo.errors.DuplicateKeyError.

rewards_earn.py::_cap_progress uses `$sum: $delta` for used-vs-cap comparison, but daily_cap_per_user in points_earn_rules is typically a POINT cap; if a rule has non-1 base_points, that's correct. Confirmed matches PointsService's cap semantics.

admin_put_catalog / admin_put_mission accept `key` / `mission_id` only in the body — no path param — so an admin editing item A can accidentally create item B by typoing the key. Consider PUT /api/admin/earn/catalog/{key} with the key in the path to enforce.
